historical_references.reference: Masud ibn Abbas, a companion of Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) and the first Qadi (judge) of Madinah. He was known for his knowledge in Islamic law and jurisprudence. Masud ibn Abbas was a cousin of Ali ibn Abi Talib, the fourth caliph of Islam.
historical_references.time_period: 622 AD - 652 AD (Prophet Muhammad's lifetime to the second caliphate of Umar ibn Al-Khattab)
historical_references.context: Early Islamic history, formation of Islamic legal system under Prophet Muhammad's guidance and the role of companions in establishing Islamic jurisprudence.

historical_references.reference: Sultan Al-Masud Shah, the last independent Sultan of Bengal. He ruled Bengal from 1236 AD to 1260 AD during the Mongol invasion of Bengal. Al-Masud Shah is known for his courage and resistance against the Mongols and is considered a symbol of Bengali national pride.
historical_references.context: Medieval Islamic history, resistance against foreign invasions and the role of local rulers in preserving Islamic culture and identity.
